Residents return north on foot after ceasefire deal

Tens of thousands of people began walking back to their towns on Monday, carrying what belongings they could, after negotiators agreed to extend the ceasefire for another week.

Many found their streets badly damaged. Aid groups said they were setting up water points and temporary shelters along the main road, but warned that supplies would run short within days without more deliveries.

Officials on both sides described the agreement as fragile and said the next round of talks would focus on reopening crossings for trucks.
